rows.acceptance: An anchored Mercenary Den tracks development and anarchy levels; high unmitigated anarchy reduces the host Skyhook's planetary workforce output until the Mercenary Den owner completes Mercenary Tactical Operations or the den is destroyed.
rows.title: Mercenary Den anarchy & development levels and Skyhook workforce impact
rows.why_missing: feat:sovereignty.mercenary-den mentions anchoring and infomorph generation, omitting development/anarchy progression and its workforce penalty on the host Skyhook.

rows.acceptance: Lava and Ice planet Skyhooks split extracted Magmatic Gas / Superionic Ice between a secure bay and an insecure (maturing) bay; reagent theft via Skyhook hacking steals from the insecure bay while the remaining portion matures into the secure bay over the maturity cycle.
rows.title: Orbital Skyhook reagent maturity and secure vs insecure bay split
rows.why_missing: feat:sovereignty.sov-reagents and feat:sovereignty.skyhook-theft omit the secure vs maturing bay split and maturity cycle.

rows.acceptance: FW Battlefield sites contain 3 capture zones that must be held by militia players to advance the battlefield progress bar, spawn friendly/enemy NPC waves, and award LP/standing to up to 30 militia pilots in site upon completion while heavily shifting system contested/advantage state.
rows.title: Faction Warfare Battlefield capture zones and payout scaling
rows.why_missing: feat:fw.fw-site-dungeons only checks GetFactionWarfareBattlefieldInstances list RPC, omitting the 3-capture-zone battlefield mechanics and 30-pilot LP payout.

rows.acceptance: Supply Caches and Supply Depots spawn in FW warzone systems; destroying enemy caches/depots or defending friendly ones adjusts system Advantage (OnSolarsystemAdvantageStateUpdated_Local) and drops militia supply items.
rows.title: Faction Warfare Supply Caches and Supply Depots
rows.why_missing: feat:fw.advantage mentions 'adjacency and structures' without covering FW Supply Caches and Supply Depots.

rows.acceptance: Each Pirate Insurgency campaign anchors a Pirate Forward Operating Base (FOB) in the insurgency headquarters system; as systems reach Stage 5 Corruption or Stage 5 Suppression, campaign points accrue until either the pirate FOB becomes vulnerable/destroyed or the insurgency wins and spawns the Pirate Stronghold / Zarzakh rewards.
rows.title: Pirate Insurgency Forward Operating Base (FOB) and Corruption/Suppression stage thresholds
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.insurgency and feat:fw.fw-pirate omit the Pirate FOB lifecycle and Stage 1-5 Corruption/Suppression campaign resolution.

rows.acceptance: In solar systems that reach Corruption Stage 3-5 during a Pirate Insurgency, low-sec gate/station sentry guns disable, high-sec CONCORD response is suppressed at Stage 5, and warp disruption bubbles / bombs become legal to deploy in low-sec at Stage 5.
rows.title: Corruption Stage 3-5 crimewatch and interdiction changes
rows.why_missing: feat:crimewatch.security-bands and feat:pve.insurgency do not test the Stage 3-5 Corruption overrides to sentry guns, CONCORD response, and bubble/bomb restrictions.

rows.acceptance: Stargates into Zarzakh apply the Deathless horizon/lockout timer preventing immediate back-jump to a different exit gate, enforce Zarzakh's directional-scanner range cap and ship size/bubble rules, and dock at The Fulcrum.
rows.title: Zarzakh Jovian stargates, horizon restriction, and Fulcrum mechanics
rows.why_missing: Zarzakh stargate lockout timers, d-scan range cap, and The Fulcrum rules have no feature row in navigation.

rows.acceptance: Shipcaster beacons in Turnur, Alsavoinon, Hikkoken and Vard allow jumping into Zarzakh via shipcasterTravelMgr with faction/capital ship restrictions and Horizon Siege timer rules.
rows.title: Deathless Shipcaster travel to Zarzakh
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.shipcaster only covers faction militia Shipcaster travel to FW landing pads (GetFactionLandingPads); the Deathless Shipcaster network into Zarzakh has no row.

rows.acceptance: Zarzakh enforces delayed local chat, prohibits capsuleer structure anchoring and cynosural fields, and gates stargate/shipcaster access per the Fulcrum and Horizon Siege state.
rows.title: Zarzakh system rules and Horizon Siege state
rows.why_missing: feat:social.chat-local mentions Zarzakh local chat in passing, but Zarzakh's stargate/shipcaster lockouts, structure/cyno restrictions, and Horizon Siege state have no dedicated row.

rows.acceptance: Capital Micro Jump Drive and Capital Micro Jump Field Generator spool up (affected by Capital Micro Jump Drive skill) and jump capital/subcapital ships forward 100-250 km; warp scramblers and HIC scripts cancel activation.
rows.title: Capital Micro Jump Drive and Capital Micro Jump Field Generator
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.micro-jump-drive only covers subcapital 100 km MJD/MJFG (12s spool); capital MJD and Capital Micro Jump Field Generator on dreadnoughts/carriers have distinct spool, range and mass rules and no row.

rows.acceptance: Special edition hulls (e.g. Metamorphosis, Sunesis, Gnosis, Praxis) apply their role-based scanning, hacking, warp stability and specialized hold bonuses from SDE dogma effects without skill scaling.
rows.title: Metamorphosis and special hull integrated role traits
rows.why_missing: feat:dogma.dogma-effects-ships covers standard skill-scaled hull bonuses, while special edition hulls with flat role bonuses and integrated traits have no dedicated test row.

rows.acceptance: Micro Jump Field Generator (Command Destroyers) jumps at most 25 non-scrambled ships, drones and probes within 6 km radius 100 km forward along the caster's heading vector; tethered, sieged, triaged, bastioned or industrial-cored ships are not moved.
rows.title: Micro Jump Field Generator 25-ship cap and immobility exclusions
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.micro-jump-drive bundles MJD and 'field variant jumps nearby ships' into one sentence, hiding the 25-ship cap, 6 km radius, drone/probe displacement, and immobility/tether exclusions.

rows.acceptance: Tenebrex Cyno Jammer Flex structure requires the sovereignty upgrade online, takes 5 minutes to spool up system-wide cyno jamming (beyonce.GetCynoJammerState), and immediately ceases jamming when reinforced into armor or hull.
rows.title: Tenebrex Cyno Jammer structure spool-up and reinforcement disable
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.cyno-jammer and feat:sovereignty.sov-cyno-jammer-upgrade do not cover the Tenebrex structure's 5-minute activation spool-up or its deactivation when reinforced.

rows.acceptance: Auto Targeting System high-slot module passively adds +2/+3 maximum locked targets and when activated locks hostile targets within targeting range automatically.
rows.title: Auto Targeting System passive target cap and active auto-lock
rows.why_missing: No row covers the Auto Targeting System module's dual passive (+maxLockedTargets) and active (auto-lock) behavior.

rows.acceptance: Passive Targeter module locks a target with a lock-time penalty without sending an OnTarget targeted-by notification (yellow-box) to the locked ship.
rows.title: Passive Targeter stealth lock without yellow-boxing
rows.why_missing: feat:dogma.targeting-lock requires OnTarget notifications to the target, missing the Passive Targeter mechanic that suppresses the target's lock warning.

rows.acceptance: Survey Probe Launcher loads Quest/Discovery/Gaze Moon Survey Probes, launches a probe toward a targeted moon (scanMgr), and delivers OnMoonScanComplete after the probe's flight/analysis timer.
rows.title: Survey Probe Launcher and Moon Survey Probe analysis timers
rows.why_missing: feat:scanning.moon-survey-probe states the outcome (OnMoonScanComplete) without covering the Survey Probe Launcher module, probe types, and per-probe analysis timer.

rows.acceptance: Faction/special combat drones (Gecko, Augmented, Integrated, Subverted) deal split multi-type damage (omni or primary+secondary damage attributes) per cycle using their SDE dogma attributes and consume 50 Mbit/s (Gecko) bandwidth.
rows.title: Gecko and Augmented/Subverted multi-damage drone attacks
rows.why_missing: feat:drones.engage-target only checks single-damage drone attacks; multi-damage-attribute drones (Integrated/Augmented/Gecko) require summing all four EM/Thermal/Kinetic/Explosive dogma attributes on drone attack cycles.

rows.acceptance: Support fighter squadrons apply warp disruption (Siren), stasis webification (Dromi), energy neutralization (Cenobite), and ECM (Scarab) scaled by surviving squadron size (fighterMgr.CmdActivateAbilitySlots).
rows.title: Support fighter EWAR squadrons (Cenobite, Scarab, Siren, Dromi)
rows.why_missing: feat:drones.fighter-abilities lists abilities in one coarse row without testing support fighter EWAR scaling by current squadron member count.

rows.acceptance: Space superiority light fighters (Equite, Gram, Locust, Satyr) apply their anti-fighter missile volley and Evasive Maneuvers speed/signature reduction ability with cooldown (fighterMgr).
rows.title: Space superiority fighter anti-fighter bonus and evasive maneuvers
rows.why_missing: No row covers Space Superiority fighters' anti-fighter abilities and Evasive Maneuvers ability slot.

rows.acceptance: Standup Point Defense Battery on XL structures deals omni AoE pulse damage within its short-range radius around the structure (structureControl), hitting all hostile ships, drones and fighters in range.
rows.title: Standup Point Defense Battery AoE pulse weapon
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.structure-weapons bundles all structure weapons into one coarse row without separate verification of Standup Point Defense Battery AoE mechanics.

rows.acceptance: Standup Guided Bomb Launcher fires light/heavy guided bombs at locked targets that detonate on impact for AoE damage scaled by target signature radius (structureControl).
rows.title: Standup Guided Bomb Launcher AoE projectile
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.structure-weapons coarsens guided bombs, AoE neut/ECM, point defense, and missiles into one row.

rows.acceptance: Keepstar Standup Arcing Vorton Projector fires a beam that chains massive omni damage across up to 5 targets within jump radius while immobilizing the gunner's weapon cycle (structureControl).
rows.title: Keepstar Standup Arcing Vorton Projector superweapon
rows.why_missing: No row covers the Keepstar-exclusive Standup Arcing Vorton Projector superweapon.

rows.acceptance: At most one Upwell Palatine Keepstar may be anchored across the entire cluster at any time; structureDeployment.Anchor rejects a second Palatine Keepstar while one exists.
rows.title: Upwell Palatine Keepstar cluster-wide uniqueness rule
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.anchor-restrictions mentions per-system limits, missing the cluster-wide singleton restriction on the Upwell Palatine Keepstar.

rows.acceptance: Standup M-Set and L-Set reprocessing rigs on Athanor and Tatara refineries apply different base yield bonuses for Asteroid Ore, Ice, and Moon Ore scaled by high-sec (1.0x), low-sec (1.06x) and null-sec/WH (1.12x) security multipliers.
rows.title: Refinery reprocessing rig security-band multipliers
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.reprocessing-yield and feat:structures.service-reprocessing do not test the security-band multiplier differences and ore/ice/moon-ore rig split on Athanor vs Tatara.

rows.acceptance: Capital ship blueprints (Dreadnoughts, Carriers, FAX, Rorqual, Jump Freighters) require the Standup Capital Shipyard service in low/null/WH space, and Supercarriers/Titans require a Sotiyo with Standup Supercapital Shipyard in sovereignty null-sec with the Supercapital Construction Facilities upgrade online.
rows.title: Capital ship construction and Standup Capital/Supercapital Shipyard gating
rows.why_missing: feat:industry.manufacturing and feat:structures.service-industry do not cover Capital Shipyard vs Supercapital Shipyard service and sovereignty upgrade requirements.

rows.acceptance: A Blueprint Original (BPO) with ME > 0 or TE > 0 cannot be repackaged into a market-sellable stack unless the player explicitly confirms resetting its ME/TE research to 0 (repackagingSvc.RepackageItems).
rows.title: Blueprint Original repackaging restriction when researched
rows.why_missing: feat:ships.repackage covers ships and modules, missing the BPO research-loss repackaging rule required before listing a BPO on the regional market.

rows.acceptance: marketProxy.PlaceMultiSellOrder accepts a batch of items with individual durations/prices, validates each item's market eligibility and repackaged state, and deducts individual broker fees and sales taxes atomically.
rows.title: Multi-sell order batching and per-item fee accounting
rows.why_missing: feat:market.place-sell only describes listing items at a station without covering multi-item batch validation, immediate-match vs sell-order split in PlaceMultiSellOrder, and repackaged-only enforcement.

rows.acceptance: marketProxy.BuyMultipleItems matches requested quantities across multiple typeIDs at the station/structure against the cheapest available sell orders, returning partial/unfilled statuses per type when supply or ISK is insufficient.
rows.title: Multibuy batch purchase across multiple types
rows.why_missing: feat:market.instant-buy does not cover multi-type batch purchasing (BuyMultipleItems) with partial availability handling.

rows.acceptance: Contracting BPOs and BPCs via contractProxy exposes each blueprint's copy flag, materialEfficiency, timeEfficiency and runs in GetContractInfo / SearchContracts and preserves them upon contract acceptance.
rows.title: Blueprint copy/original ME/TE/runs preservation in contracts
rows.why_missing: feat:contracts.item-exchange and feat:contracts.search do not test blueprint instance metadata (BPC vs BPO, ME, TE, remaining runs) in contract inspection and search.

rows.acceptance: Pirate Forward Operating Bases spawn in high/low-sec systems, launch raiding fleets and defending responses scaled to attacking player fleet composition, and drop structure loot and bounties on destruction.
rows.title: Blood Raider and Guristas Forward Operating Bases (FOB)
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.npc-mining-ops covers belt mining NPCs, but Pirate Forward Operating Bases (FOBs) that spawn those ops and scale defense fleets have no row.

rows.acceptance: Activating an Abyssal filament leaves a warpable/scannable Abyssal Trace in the origin solar system until the pilot exits or dies; exiting high-tier filaments in high-sec applies a 15-minute Suspect flag per V24 tier/security rules.
rows.title: Abyssal trace persistence in space and high-sec suspect timer
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.filament-abyssal and feat:pve.abyssal-pocket do not cover the persistent Abyssal Trace left in the origin system or the high-tier high-sec suspect flag.

rows.acceptance: Observatory Flashpoint sites in Pochven require fleet composition/standing access, spawn Triglavian/EDENCOM defense waves and Dreadnought/World Ark bosses, and pay collective ISK and DED/Triglavian LP to up to 15 fleet members.
rows.title: Pochven Observatory Flashpoint sites and World Ark
rows.why_missing: feat:npc.triglavians and feat:navigation.pochven-travel do not cover Pochven's signature PvE content: Observatory Flashpoint sites and their 15-pilot payout mechanics.

rows.acceptance: Characters in NPC starter/school corporations pay the fixed 11% NPC corporation tax on NPC bounty ticks and agent mission ISK/LP rewards above the minimum taxable threshold (100,000 ISK), recorded in the wallet journal.
rows.title: NPC corporation 11% ISK and LP tax deduction
rows.why_missing: feat:corporation.corp-tax covers player-corporation tax credited to the corp master wallet, missing the 11% NPC corporation sink tax and threshold rule.

rows.acceptance: Chat messages containing showinfo:, fitting:, killReport:, bookmarkFolder: and overviewPreset: links preserve their payloads through chat / mailMgr and resolve via their respective server handlers when clicked by recipients.
rows.title: In-game chat hyperlinks for items, fittings, killmails, bookmarks and overview profiles
rows.why_missing: Individual services exist in scattered rows, but chat/mail hyperlink preservation and server resolution across the 5 interactive link schemes has no row.

rows.acceptance: ESI GET /corporations/{corporation_id}/structures/ returns each owned Upwell structure's state, fuel_expires, state_timer_start/state_timer_end, reinforce_hour, next_reinforce_hour/next_reinforce_apply, and online services list reflecting live server structure state.
rows.title: ESI GET /corporations/{corporation_id}/structures state, fuel expires, and reinforcement schedule
rows.why_missing: esi:GET /corporations/{corporation_id}/structures has no companion feat:esi.* row verifying that structure reinforcement timers, fuel expiry, and service states match the live Upwell structure state machine.

rows.acceptance: Each W-space system with a phenomenon applies its effect set to capsuleer ships only (not Sleepers or structures), at the system's class strength. Pulsar: shield HP, signature radius and neut/nos amount +30/44/58/72/86/100%; armor resists and cap recharge time -15..-50%. Black Hole: ship velocity, targeting range and missile explosion velocity +30..+100%; missile velocity and inertia +15..+50%; web strength -15..-50%. Cataclysmic Variable: remote armor/shield rep and capacitor capacity +30..+100%; local reps and remote cap transmitter -15..-50%; cap recharge time +15..+50%. Magnetar: damage and missile explosion radius +30..+100%; tracking, drone tracking, targeting range and painter strength -15..-50%. Red Giant: heat damage +15..+50%; overload bonus, smartbomb range/damage and bomb damage +30..+100%. Wolf-Rayet: armor HP +30..+100%; shield resists and signature -15..-50%; small weapon damage +60..+200%. C13 systems use C6 Wolf-Rayet values. Drifter wormhole systems use C2 strength. The effect is shown in the system-wide effects HUD.
rows.title: Wormhole system phenomena effects by class
rows.why_missing: feat:dogma.system-wide-effects lumps wormhole effects, Pochven, insurgency and storms into one sentence with no phenomenon list or magnitudes, so 36 class/phenomenon combinations have no testable row.

rows.acceptance: The 25 J000xxx systems only connect through small-ship wormholes that admit frigates, destroyers, Porpoise and mass-qualified HIC/Odysseus. They spawn C1-C3 sites, apply C6 Wolf-Rayet effects and spawn signatures and anomalies more often than normal systems.
rows.title: Small-ship shattered (C13) wormhole systems
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.wormhole-thera bundles Thera, shattered and Drifter systems into one coarse sentence. C13 hull restrictions and effects are untestable as written.

rows.acceptance: Shattered systems behave as follows: no moons; Upwell anchoring is refused; they get one K-space static beyond their class statics (C4s use C3-type K-space statics); they spawn sites of their own class plus or minus one; each has one Shattered Debris Field and one Shattered Ice Field (the only ice in J-space), each guarded by a single delayed Sleeper wave.
rows.title: Standard shattered wormhole system rules
rows.why_missing: No row covers shattered-system statics, the anchoring ban or the unique ore/ice fields. wormhole-thera only says 'behave per rules'.

rows.acceptance: There are five Drifter systems: J200727, J164710, J174618, J055520 and J110145. Each has around 50-70 K-space connections and six statics to C1-C6 (Z647, D382, O477, Y683, N062, R474), and every signature in them is a wormhole. On the K-space side the connection is an 'unidentified wormhole' beacon that needs no scanning, with types C414, V928, R259, S877 and B735. Both sides are deadspace, so warping in lands about 80 km off. Drifter battleships guard the K-space side. System effects are at C2 strength.
rows.title: Drifter wormhole systems and unidentified wormholes
rows.why_missing: No row defines the Drifter wormhole network, its beacon-type K-space entrances or its static set. npc.drifters and pve.drifter-hives cover different content.

rows.acceptance: When a dreadnought or carrier warps into a C5/C6 combat anomaly or Sleeper data/relic site, Upgraded Avenger battleships spawn: 3 per capital in C5, 4 per capital in C6. They have a 30,000 m signature and web, scram and neut. Each capital type can trigger at most two escalations (four in total), and waves regenerate after downtime. Escalation NPCs despawn when the capital leaves or moves more than 100 km from the warp-in.
rows.title: C5/C6 capital escalation waves
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.wormhole-sites is a single coarse row with no capital-trigger, scaling, cap or despawn rules.

rows.acceptance: Finishing a C5/C6 combat or Sleeper data/relic site spawns a Decloaked Transmission Relay. Attacking it spawns Arithmos Tyrannos if a capital was on grid when the relay spawned, otherwise Hyleus Tyrannos. Both have warp core strength 3, scram, web and neut, and warp around the system if not killed. Arithmos drops Sleeper loot.
rows.title: Decloaked Transmission Relay / Drifter response battleship
rows.why_missing: No ledger row mentions the Transmission Relay or the Drifter response escalation.

rows.acceptance: A W-space site that has been activated (first warp-in) despawns at the third downtime after activation if completed, and at the fourth if left unfinished.
rows.title: W-space site despawn by downtime count
rows.why_missing: feat:scanning.sig-despawn says only that 'completed/expired sites despawn'. The downtime-count rule for W-space has no row.

rows.acceptance: Selected NPC stations carry permanent buy orders for Sleeper components at fixed prices: Neural Network Analyzer 200,000 ISK, Sleeper Data Library 500,000 ISK, Ancient Coordinates Database 1,500,000 ISK, Sleeper Drone AI Nexus 5,000,000 ISK. Selling into them goes through normal market matching and sales tax, and the orders never deplete.
rows.title: NPC buy orders for Sleeper components (blue loot)
rows.why_missing: feat:market.npc-seed-orders covers NPC sell orders only. Permanent NPC buy orders, the only outlet for blue loot, have no row.

rows.acceptance: Player neutralizers have no effect on Sleeper NPCs; a nosferatu still gains energy for the user without draining the Sleeper. Sleepers that are pulled about 200 km from their spawn point teleport back.
rows.title: Sleeper infinite capacitor and spawn leash
rows.why_missing: feat:npc.sleepers is one line ('Sleeper AI ... with remote reps'), with no capacitor immunity or leash behaviour.

rows.acceptance: Sleepers deal EM/Thermal beam and Explosive/Kinetic missile damage, neut (about 40 km for cruisers, 20 km for frigates) and web. They warp-scramble only in C3 and higher, deal extra damage to capital ships, and remote-repair each other in higher classes.
rows.title: Sleeper EWAR and anti-capital damage by class
rows.why_missing: Class-dependent Sleeper EWAR (scramble only in C3+) and anti-capital damage are not covered by any npc row.

rows.acceptance: Vigilant, Wakeful and Restless Sleeper sentries in W-space sites fire every 15 s for EM/Thermal damage out to 250 km and have a 50 m signature radius, with stats taken from the SDE NPC types.
rows.title: Sleeper sentry towers
rows.why_missing: No row covers Sleeper site sentries. npc.sentry-guns is about empire gate/station sentries.

rows.acceptance: Hypnosian Sleepers in Pochven spawn on celestials, ore anomalies, wormholes and Torpid Sleeper Hive sites in three tiers: Faded, normal, and Aroused (which has a shield layer). They drop Interstellar Navigation Logs instead of blue loot, and the logs can be traded at Triglavian stations.
rows.title: Pochven Hypnosian Sleepers and navigation logs
rows.why_missing: No Pochven row covers Hypnosian Sleepers or the navigation-log loot replacement.

rows.acceptance: A newly spawned wormhole's destination-side K162 signature does not exist until a ship first jumps through. After that it appears in the destination system's signatures and is probeable there.
rows.title: K162 exit appears only after first transit
rows.why_missing: wormhole-jump and wormhole-statics do not cover the delayed creation of the K162 side.

rows.acceptance: Any skill with an NPC-seeded sell order can be bought and injected directly from the skills UI from any location, at 130% of the NPC price. ISK is debited and journaled, the skill is added at level 0, and skills without NPC-seeded orders are refused.
rows.title: Buy and inject skill from the character sheet
rows.why_missing: skills rows cover injecting a skillbook item only. The remote buy-and-inject path at a 30% markup has no row.

rows.acceptance: An Alpha character's training queue is disabled once trained SP plus unallocated SP reaches 5,000,000 and cannot be unpaused. Unallocated SP can still be applied to skills. Omega status removes the limit.
rows.title: Alpha queue disabled at 5M total SP
rows.why_missing: feat:skills.alpha-skill-caps is about per-skill alpha caps. The total-SP queue lockout, which counts unallocated SP, has no row.

rows.acceptance: Omega accounts can claim a free 15,000 SP offer in the New Eden Store once per week. The offer refreshes at Tuesday downtime, credits unallocated SP and is refused for Alpha accounts or a second claim in the same week.
rows.title: Weekly free 15,000 SP for Omega
rows.why_missing: wallet.nes-store covers generic offer purchase. The recurring weekly SP grant and its reset rule are untested.

rows.acceptance: New characters start with Int/Per/Wil/Mem 20 and Cha 19 (99 total, 14 remappable), and each base attribute stays within 17-27. A new character has one normal remap plus two bonus remaps. The normal remap is consumed before bonus remaps and replenishes after one year.
rows.title: Starting attributes and remap consumption order
rows.why_missing: feat:attributes.neural-remap and bonus-remap do not specify the 19-Charisma default, the 14-point pool, or that the normal remap is used first.

rows.acceptance: Booster and cerebral accelerator duration increases by 20% per Biology level (doubled at V). Expiry and the attribute bonus end at the extended time.
rows.title: Biology extends booster/accelerator duration
rows.why_missing: booster-consume and skills.accelerators do not mention the Biology duration modifier.

rows.acceptance: The broker fee and relist fee each have a 100 ISK minimum. Upwell market orders pay a fixed 0.5% SCC surcharge plus the owner rate (owner minimum 0%), unaffected by skills. Immediate-duration orders pay no broker fee.
rows.title: Broker fee minimum, SCC structure surcharge, immediate orders
rows.why_missing: feat:market.broker-fee mentions only the NPC formula or 'structure owner fee'. The minimum fee, the SCC surcharge and the immediate-order exemption are untested.

rows.acceptance: Player orders accept only the client duration set (immediate, 1, 3, 7, 14, 30, 90 days); durations over 90 days are rejected. NPC-seeded orders carry about one year of expiry.
rows.title: Market order duration limits
rows.why_missing: order-expiry tests expiry only. Validation of allowed durations and the 90-day cap has no row.

rows.acceptance: Co-Processors raise CPU by a percentage. Reactor Control Units and Micro Auxiliary Power Cores raise powergrid by a percentage or flat amount. Power Diagnostic Systems give shield/cap/PG bonuses. Ancillary current routers and processor overclocking rigs apply. CPU/PG bonuses are not stacking-penalized, per SDE stackable flags.
rows.title: CPU/PG capacity modules and rigs
rows.why_missing: No modules row covers fitting-capacity upgrades. cap-mods and damage-mods are unrelated families.

rows.acceptance: Expanded Cargohold modules increase cargo capacity while reducing max velocity and structure HP, with stacking applied per SDE. Cargo Optimization rigs increase capacity at the cost of their drawback. Cargo moves respect the modified capacity.
rows.title: Expanded cargoholds and cargo rigs
rows.why_missing: ships.cargo-capacity checks volume limits only. The capacity-modifying modules and their drawbacks have no row.

rows.acceptance: Drone Damage Amplifiers raise drone damage with stacking penalty. Drone Navigation Computers raise drone MWD velocity. Omnidirectional Tracking Links/Enhancers with scripts raise drone optimal/tracking. Drone Link Augmentors raise drone control range. All apply only to drones launched from the fitted ship.
rows.title: Drone damage amplifiers, navigation computers and tracking links
rows.why_missing: Drone rows cover launching, recall and bandwidth. The drone upgrade module family has no row.

rows.acceptance: GetSkillHistory returns one row per training completion, injection, extraction and removal, with logDate, skillTypeID, skillLevel and absolutePoints, in chronological order, kept across relog.
rows.title: Skill history event rows
rows.why_missing: feat:skills.skill-history is marked DONE with a test that only checks column names. This row pins the per-event content so it can be tested separately.

rows.acceptance: A buy order placed with range station, solar system, 1-40 jumps or region can be filled by a seller at any station inside that range. Items are delivered at the seller's station, and sellers outside the range cannot match. The Visibility level (0 station, 1 system, 2: 5 jumps, 3: 10, 4: 20, 5 region) caps the range allowed at placement.
rows.title: Sellers fill buy orders anywhere within order range
rows.why_missing: remote-orders covers where orders can be placed. Range-based matching from the seller's station, and delivery at that station, has no testable row.

rows.acceptance: Within a single C5/C6 site, escalation triggers are counted per capital class (dreadnought vs carrier/FAX). The third trigger by the same class spawns nothing, and the counter resets at downtime.
rows.title: Capital escalation trigger cap per site
rows.why_missing: The two-per-capital-type cap is a separately testable rule apart from wave composition. No row covers it.

rows.acceptance: Thera (31000005) is the only W-space system with NPC stations: four dockable Sisters of EVE stations with market, clone and other services, and normal docking rules apply. Wormhole connections to Thera spawn from K-space and W-space.
rows.title: Thera Sisters of EVE stations
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.wormhole-thera bundles Thera into a generic 'no structures, special effects' clause. Thera's NPC station services and docking have no testable row.

rows.acceptance: Burst strength = charge base bonus x (1+Specialist skill) x (1+module, T2 = +25%) x (1+ship bonus) x (1+mindlink) x (1+Industrial Core bonus, applied only to Mining Foreman bursts from Porpoise/Orca/Rorqual). T2 bursts need the burst's Specialist skill. The strongest buff of each type applies and the value reaches the fleet member's dogma attributes.
rows.title: Command burst strength formula
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.command-bursts says only 'burst charges apply fleet dbuffs ... with duration'. The multiplicative strength chain, the T2 +25% and the core-only-for-mining rule are not testable from it.

rows.acceptance: Range = 15 km x (1+7%/lvl Leadership) x (1+6%/lvl Wing Command) x (1+5%/lvl Fleet Command) x (1+ship range bonus, e.g. +200% capital, +100% Fleet Command Ship, +50% Orca/Rorqual/BC/T3C) x (1+Industrial Core bonus, Porpoise/Orca/Rorqual only). Only fleet members inside the range receive the buff, up to 256 members.
rows.title: Command burst area-of-effect range
rows.why_missing: feat:fleet.fleet-boost-scope and feat:modules.command-bursts give no range formula or skill multipliers.

rows.acceptance: Buff duration = 60 s x (1+10%/lvl racial Command skill) x (1+ship duration bonus) x (1+mindlink); the buff persists for that duration after the pulse. Charge reload time = 60 s x (1 - 0.1 x Command Burst Specialist), so 30 s at level V.
rows.title: Command burst buff duration and charge reload
rows.why_missing: No ledger or auditor row fixes the burst duration or reload formulas.

rows.acceptance: Command bursts fit only on Capital Industrial Ships, Carriers, Combat Battlecruisers, Command Destroyers, Command Ships, Force Auxiliaries, Industrial Command Ships, Strategic Cruisers, Supercarriers and Titans (SDE canFitShipGroup/Type). Activation requires Omega, but any clone state receives the effect. Each Command Processor I rig (150 calibration) allows one more burst module.
rows.title: Command burst fitting and Omega restrictions
rows.why_missing: No row covers the hull whitelist, the Omega activation gate or the Command Processor rig.

rows.acceptance: While active, an Industrial Core raises command burst range by Medium 45%/60%, Large 75%/100% and Capital 200%/250% (T1/T2), and raises Mining Foreman burst strength. The Orca and Rorqual also get +50% burst range and +5% per ship-skill level to Mining Foreman burst range, applied multiplicatively.
rows.title: Industrial core command burst bonuses
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.industrial-core says only 'enables boosts/compression, makes ship immobile'. The per-size range table and the mining-strength bonus are absent.

rows.title: Bastion module V24 effects
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.bastion-module says 'immune to EWAR', which contradicts V24 (ECM immunity was removed in 19.06 and damp/TD/TP resistances in Viridian). The per-attribute effects and the 2025 repair changes are untested.

rows.acceptance: A bastioned Marauder can jump a wormhole and arrives with Bastion deactivated. Micro Jump Drive activation is refused while Bastion is active, but a Command Destroyer MJFG still moves the bastioned ship.
rows.title: Bastion vs wormhole jump and MJD/MJFG
rows.why_missing: Neither the bastion row nor the MJFG rows cover these interactions.

rows.title: Entosis link activation restrictions
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.entosis-link is one line ('contested during vulnerability; prevents cloaking/warp'). The fuel, capital penalties, speed cap and interceptor ban are untested.

rows.acceptance: The first cycle is a warm-up with no effect, and losing lock restarts it. When the warm-up completes, the owning alliance is notified. Capture time depends on the structure's base timer and the ADM, not on the link's cycle time. Extra links from the same side do not speed up capture, and any active link from another side (allies included) pauses the timer.
rows.title: Entosis warm-up cycle and contest rules
rows.why_missing: No ledger or auditor row defines the warm-up cycle, the owner notification or the multi-link and contest semantics.

rows.acceptance: Jumping to an inactive clone stored in the same NPC station or Upwell structure incurs no clone-jump cooldown and is allowed while a cooldown is running. Jumping to any other location starts the 24 h (minus 1 h per Infomorph Synchronizing level) cooldown.
rows.title: No cooldown for same-location clone swap
rows.why_missing: feat:clones.jump-clone-jump covers the cooldown only; the same-location exemption is untested.

rows.acceptance: Clone jumps into, out of or between wormhole systems are refused, except to and from Thera, which behaves as k-space. In-structure clone swaps inside a W-space Upwell structure are allowed.
rows.title: No clone jumps into, out of or within W-space
rows.why_missing: Only the Pochven clone restriction exists (auditor row); the W-space ban and the Thera exception have no row.

rows.acceptance: A clone jump requires being docked, in a capsule (not in any ship) and with no session-change timer running. Leaving the current body behind at an NPC station costs 900,000 ISK, debited and journaled. At an Upwell structure the owner sets the fee per standing, minimum 1 ISK. Infomorph Psychology I is required for any clone action.
rows.title: Clone jump preconditions and leave-behind fee
rows.why_missing: feat:clones.jump-clone-install covers only the installation fee; the jump-time preconditions and the leave-behind fee are untested.

rows.acceptance: Alpha characters can jump between jump clones that were created while Omega. They are refused when the action would need Omega-only capacity per V24 rules.
rows.title: Alpha clones and existing jump clones
rows.why_missing: No clones row addresses clone-state gating.

rows.acceptance: On a clone jump, skills, standings, corporation membership and active cerebral accelerator effects transfer to the new body. Implants stay in the old body, which becomes a jump clone. Active boosters and their side effects are removed.
rows.title: What transfers on a clone jump
rows.why_missing: feat:clones.jump-clone-jump tests the implant swap only; booster removal and accelerator persistence are untested.

rows.acceptance: Mission LP reward = base LP x (1.6288 - the agent system's true security) x (1 + 0.1 x the matching division Connections skill: Distribution, Mining or Security). The ISK reward is +5% per Negotiation level. Both are credited and journaled on completion.
rows.title: Mission LP/ISK reward scaling
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.mission-complete and mission-levels do not specify the true-security LP multiplier or the division-Connections and Negotiation modifiers.

rows.acceptance: Accepting a mission starts a bonus timer of 10 min to 6 h, per mission data. Completing before it expires pays the bonus reward in addition to the normal reward; completing after it pays the normal reward only.
rows.title: Mission time bonus reward
rows.why_missing: No pve row mentions the bonus timer or the conditional bonus reward.

rows.acceptance: An un-accepted mission offer is withdrawn 6-7 days after the conversation, with the agent's expiry message and no standing change. COSMOS offers that expire are never re-offered, and neither are their follow-ups. A failed 7-day completion timer applies agent, corp and faction penalties.
rows.title: Mission offer expiry without penalty
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.mission-expire does not distinguish the penalty-free offer timer from the completion timer, or cover the COSMOS one-shot rule.

rows.acceptance: Alpha clones may accept missions up to level 3; level 4 and 5 offers need Omega. Level 5 agents exist only in low-sec. Refusals use the live error.
rows.title: Mission level clone and security restrictions
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.mission-levels and mission-standing-gate gate by standing only, not by clone state.

rows.acceptance: Every 16 completed missions of the same level and faction trigger a Storyline offer of that level from the nearest Storyline agent of that faction. The offer comes from the second-nearest agent if the nearest already has a pending offer, and is always from a high-sec agent if the 16th mission's agent was in high-sec. InterBus and militia corps never generate offers.
rows.title: Storyline offer every 16 missions
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.mission-storyline does not fix the 16-mission counter, the agent selection or the exclusions.

rows.acceptance: A paid insurance contract lasts 12 weeks. Repackaging, trading, selling, contracting or moving the ship into a corporation hangar voids it, as does a CONCORD kill in high-sec; a voided ship falls back to the default 40% payout. A loss pays out immediately and sends an EVE-mail.
rows.title: Insurance voiding and 12-week expiry
rows.why_missing: feat:combat.insurance-buy/payout do not cover the void triggers or the 12-week validity.

rows.acceptance: A character keeps at most 3,000 player mails, counting mailing-list and Trash mails; beyond that, older mails are no longer listed until some are deleted. Notifications are capped at 500. Mail body length is limited to 8,000 characters including formatting markup.
rows.title: Mailbox and notification caps
rows.why_missing: The social mail rows cover send/read/labels/trash but not the mailbox caps or body length.

rows.acceptance: Each NPC station's reprocessing equipment has its own base yield (30-50%, from data). The NPC reprocessing tax is 5% at 0 standing, falling linearly to 0% at 6.67 standing, using the higher of personal and corporation standing with the station owner. Connections applies only after at least one mission for that corp.
rows.title: NPC station reprocessing equipment and tax curve
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.reprocessing-tax says only 'depends on NPC standings'; the 5%-to-0% curve, the max-of-standings rule and per-station equipment yields are untested.

rows.acceptance: Reprocessing ships, modules and other non-ore items yields facility base x (1 + 0.02 x Scrapmetal Processing). Upwell structure, rig, security-band and implant bonuses never apply, so the maximum is 55% at a 50% facility.
rows.title: Scrapmetal yield ignores structure, rig, security and implant bonuses
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.reprocessing-modules names Scrapmetal Processing but not the bonus exclusions or the 55% cap.

rows.acceptance: While Bastion is active, docking, tethering and warp requests are refused with the live UserError, and they are allowed again once the module deactivates.
rows.title: Immobilizing modules block docking, tethering and warping
rows.why_missing: The navigation dock/tether/warp rows and the auditor tether-eligibility row do not list Bastion among the blockers.

rows.acceptance: Items inside any container must first be moved to the item hangar, otherwise the action is refused with the live UserError. This covers repackagingSvc.RepackageItems, the repair service, contract creation, market sell orders and deliveries. Ammunition in a container in cargo is not used for automatic reload, but a manual LoadAmmo from that container succeeds.
rows.title: Items inside containers cannot be repackaged, repaired, contracted, sold or auto-reloaded
rows.why_missing: feat:inventory.containers covers assembly, capacity and nesting only. The refusal rules for items held in containers are not covered by any row.

rows.title: Audit log / station container event log and retention lock
rows.why_missing: feat:inventory.secure-containers says only 'record access per lock settings'. The event set, the default-lock and per-action password configuration, and the 3-week trash/repackage lock have no testable row.

rows.acceptance: Anchoring a secure or audit log container needs Anchoring I and is refused in systems with security 0.8 or higher. An anchored container lasts 30 days, and opening it resets the timer. Attacking an anchored container, or an unanchored secure container in high-sec, is a criminal act that brings a CONCORD response. Anchored secure containers cannot be found with probes.
rows.title: Anchoring secure containers in space
rows.why_missing: Ledger and auditor anchoring rows cover Upwell and mobile structures only. The rules for anchoring secure containers are absent.

rows.acceptance: A packaged freight container launched from cargo or a fleet hangar assembles itself in space. It cannot be anchored or password-protected and despawns at downtime. It can be scooped only into a hold with room for the assembled volume, and it stays assembled when scooped. Freight containers are the only containers allowed assembled in freighter and jump freighter holds.
rows.title: Freight containers: launch, lifetime and scooping
rows.why_missing: feat:inventory.station-containers mentions freight containers only generically ('obey capacity/anchoring rules'). The space behaviour and freighter-hold exception are untested.

rows.acceptance: Jettisoning creates a jettison container with 55,000 m3 capacity. It can never be scooped into a hold, despawns as soon as it is emptied, and otherwise despawns when its V24 lifetime ends.
rows.title: Jettison container capacity, scoop ban and despawn
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.mining-to-jetcan covers ownership, the suspect flag and a 1h lifetime only. The 55,000 m3 capacity (doubled in 20.03), the scoop ban and empty-despawn are not covered.

rows.title: R&D agent access, skills and agent slots
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.research-agents says only 'accrue research points per day by skill/standing'. The skill gate, the RPM slot cap and the dual standing rule are not testable from it.

rows.acceptance: Research points accrue per day as RP/day = (1 + (20 + 5*Negotiation + agentStanding)/100) * (fieldSkill + agentLevel)^2. agentStanding is the personal standing with the agent, raised by Connections only after at least one mission for that agent. Accrued RP are persisted per agent and returned by the agent's research query. A level-4 agent's passive maximum is 125.55 RP per day.
rows.title: Research point accrual formula
rows.why_missing: No ledger or auditor row gives the RP formula or its inputs.

rows.acceptance: Buying datacores from an R&D agent costs 100 RP plus 10,000 ISK per datacore, of the agent's field type. ISK is debited and journaled, RP are deducted, and the datacores are delivered to the agent station hangar. The agent offers at most as many datacores as the RP balance affords.
rows.title: Datacore purchase from R&D agent
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.research-agents says only 'points redeem for datacores'. The price, the ISK fee and the delivery location are untested.

rows.acceptance: An R&D agent with active research offers one mission per day: either a short courier or a Tritanium supply mission scaled by agent level (8,100 Tritanium at level 4). Completing it adds one day's RP. Declining or ignoring it has no standing penalty and does not stop research. Completions count toward the 16-mission storyline counter.
rows.title: R&D agent daily missions
rows.why_missing: No row covers R&D agent missions, their RP reward or their exemption from decline penalties.

rows.acceptance: A ship that commands a warp enters warp on the first 1 s server tick at which it has reached 75% of max velocity in the warp direction. The effective align time is therefore ceil(ln(4)*inertia*mass/1e6) seconds; for example, a computed 3.1 s align warps out at 4 s.
rows.title: Warp entry happens on whole server ticks
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.align-to gives only the continuous align formula. Tick rounding is a separately observable rule with no row.

rows.acceptance: A cargo scanner targeting a Blockade Runner returns no cargo contents, with the live message. NPC customs contraband scans in high-sec still apply to Blockade Runners.
rows.title: Blockade Runner cargo scanner immunity
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.cargo-scanner is 'Show target cargo contents' with no immunity rule. Hull-based scan immunity has no row.

rows.acceptance: Boarding a ship whose requiredSkill1..6 the character lacks at the required level is refused, both in the hangar (ship.Board) and in space, with the live UserError. Omega-only hulls are refused to Alpha clones according to the clonegrades data. Ships the character qualifies for board normally.
rows.title: Boarding requires the ship's skills and clone state
rows.why_missing: feat:ships.board-ship covers only the session and active-ship update. No row requires skill or clone-state checks when boarding.

rows.acceptance: Strip Fitting on a docked ship moves every fitted module, loaded charge and drone-bay drone to the hangar in one operation. Rigs and T3 subsystems are left fitted. The operation is refused in space. One inventory-change batch and OnModuleUnfitted notifications are pushed.
rows.title: Strip fitting
rows.why_missing: Only single-module unfit (feat:fitting.unfit-module) exists. The bulk strip operation and its rig and subsystem exclusion have no row.

rows.acceptance: Mercoxit (and its variants) can be mined only by Deep Core Mining Lasers or Modulated Deep Core strip miners, with the Deep Core Mining skill. Ordinary mining lasers and strip miners refuse to activate on Mercoxit with the live UserError.
rows.title: Mercoxit requires deep core mining equipment
rows.why_missing: Mining rows cover generic lasers, strip miners and crystals. The Mercoxit equipment restriction is untested.

rows.title: Ice harvester cycle-time modifiers
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.ice-harvester asserts only one unit per cycle, and feat:mining.mining-upgrades covers yield upgrades. Duration modifiers for ice are absent.

rows.acceptance: Phased Asteroid Fields spawn randomly in low-sec and null-sec as signatures that must be probed. A hyperspace fracture moves across the site and breaches Phased Asteroids in its path. Breached (phased-out) asteroids yield Prismaticite at 10% efficiency until phased in. When the fracture passes halfway, a beacon spawns and the site becomes visible to everyone in system and on the star map. Asteroids collapse when the fracture moves away.
rows.title: Phased Asteroid Fields (Catalyst)
rows.why_missing: Added in the Catalyst expansion (Nov 2025). No mining, scanning or pve row mentions it.

rows.acceptance: A deployed Mobile Phase Anchor needs 100 energy from connected Industrial Command Ships: a Rorqual provides 100, an Orca 50 and a Porpoise 35. Once powered, it phases in a breached Phased Asteroid so Prismaticite is mined at 100% efficiency, until the asteroid phases out or the fracture leaves.
rows.title: Mobile Phase Anchor and ICS energy
rows.why_missing: No row covers this deployable or its ICS energy contribution.

rows.acceptance: Each reprocessing batch of Prismaticite yields one of the 8 mineral types, chosen at random, in a variable quantity. Unrefined Mineral reactions turn Compressed Prismaticite plus atmospheric gases into a chosen Unrefined Mineral; they need a Standup Composite Reactor. Unrefined Minerals reprocess into their mineral with variable output.
rows.title: Prismaticite reprocessing and Unrefined Mineral reactions
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.reprocessing-yield assumes deterministic typeMaterials. The random-batch Prismaticite rule and the Unrefined Mineral reactions are absent.

rows.title: Lancer dreadnought Disruptive Lance
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.doomsday covers Titan superweapons only. The Revenant Lancer lance and its logistics and travel denial have no row.

rows.title: Siege module V24 effect table and strontium
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.siege-module is one line ('bonuses, immobility, remote assistance immunity, cycle 5 min'). The per-attribute effects, strontium formula and weapons-timer exemption are not testable from it, mirroring the Bastion split in auditor rows.

rows.title: Triage module V24 effect table and strontium
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.triage-module is one line. The effect table, strontium consumption and EWAR lockout are untested.

rows.acceptance: Anchoring a mobile warp disruptor requires Anchoring II (Small I), III (Small II), IV (Large I) or V (Large II), checked from the type's required skills. Anchoring below the required level is refused with the live UserError.
rows.title: Mobile warp disruptor Anchoring skill tiers
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.mobile-warp-disruptor covers deployment and timers but no skill gate per size and tech level.

rows.title: Interdiction Sphere Launcher probe variants and limits
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.interdiction-sphere is one line ('spawn a warp disruption field in null/WH; prevents warp and drags'). Probe variants, lifetimes, launcher cadence, the shuttle exemption and the corruption-5 exception are absent.

rows.acceptance: A Stasis Webification Probe detonates 3 s after launch. It applies a 40% velocity reduction to every ship within 10 km for 30 s and does not disrupt warp. A second wubble on an already-affected ship resets the timer without stacking. The launcher holds 5 of these probes.
rows.title: Stasis Webification Probe (wubble)
rows.why_missing: No row mentions webification probes. feat:modules.stasis-webifier covers targeted webs only.

rows.acceptance: When an Upwell structure's manufacturing, research or reaction service module goes offline (out of fuel, low power or manual), every running job in that service pauses. Job end times are extended by the paused duration and jobs resume when the service is back online. industryManager.GetJobsByOwner reports the paused status.
rows.title: Industry jobs pause when the structure service goes offline
rows.why_missing: Industry rows cover install, cost, complete and cancel. The pause and resume behaviour tied to structure service state has no row.

rows.acceptance:
Crystal groups:
- asteroid crystals by ore tier: Simple, Coherent, Variegated, Complex, Abyssal, Mercoxit;
- moon crystals by class: Ubiquitous, Common, Uncommon, Rare, Exceptional.

A loaded crystal adds its yield bonus only when the target ore belongs to the crystal's tier or class. The match is resolved from SDE type/group data, not names. On any other ore it gives no benefit: base modulated yield, no penalty. Mission-unique ores never match.

Crystals load only into modulated (T2) ore miners and the ORE deep core laser, and need the matching resource-processing skill.
rows.title: Mining crystal ore-tier compatibility
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.modulated-crystals only says 'matching ore type', which reflects the pre-19.11 per-ore crystals. No row defines the tier/class mapping or the 'no benefit, no penalty' rule. The implementation matches crystals to ores by name substring and applies an invented 0.25x penalty (crates/eve-server/src/services/inventory_fitting.rs:3065-3080).

rows.acceptance: Type A, B and C crystals (T1 and T2) apply their SDE yield modifier, cycle-duration multiplier, residue probability and residue multiplier, matching the wiki table. Examples: Type B I has 0.9x duration and Type B II 0.8x; Type C has high residue. Each attribute changes the per-cycle result and composes correctly with skills and bursts.
rows.title: Crystal Type A/B/C yield and duration modifiers
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.mining-residue covers only residue. No row covers a crystal's cycle-duration multiplier or its per-type yield modifier. The current implementation never applies a crystal duration multiplier (crates/eve-server/src/services/inventory_fitting.rs:3182-3191).

rows.title: Upwell structure base reprocessing yield by type
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.service-reprocessing is coarse, and its test asserts Athanor = 52% (crates/eve-server/tests/mining_complete.rs:2392), contradicting the wiki. The auditor rows mining.npc-reprocessing-equipment-and-tax-curve and structures.reprocessing-rig-security-multipliers cover NPC stations and rigs only.

rows.title: Mining Foreman Burst per-charge effects
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.mining-fleet-boosts is one line ('increase yield/reduce cycle/increase range'). The implementation applies a flat 0.85 duration and 0.70 waste multiplier for any group-1771 charge (crates/eve-server/src/services/inventory_fitting.rs:3093-3153). The auditor rows command-burst-strength-formula, command-burst-range and command-burst-duration-reload are generic.

rows.acceptance: moonExtractions.StartNewExtraction accepts a player-chosen duration from 6 to 56 days, and the chunk arrives at start + duration. Chunk volume = 30,000 m³ per hour of extraction, split by the moon's survey composition fractions. CancelExtraction before arrival stops the extraction and produces no chunk.
rows.title: Moon extraction duration and chunk volume
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.moon-extraction only says 'schedules chunk arrival'. The tagged test passes no duration and assumes a fixed 6-day arrival (crates/eve-server/tests/mining_complete.rs:2542-2581). No row ties chunk volume to duration and composition.

rows.acceptance: If the owner does not fracture an arrived chunk, it detonates automatically about 3 hours after arrival and spawns the same moon ore field. Refinery rigs can change that delay. FractureChunkWithStructure before arrival is refused.
rows.title: Automatic moon chunk detonation
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.moon-fracture mentions 'or auto-fracture' only as an alternative. No row specifies the 3-hour auto-detonation or its rig modifier, and no test exercises it.

rows.title: Survey probe launch, alignment and flight time
rows.why_missing: feat:scanning.moon-survey-probe is FLAGGED_FAKE. The implementation targets a moon ID through dogmaIM.Activate and returns the composition instantly (crates/eve-server/tests/mining_complete.rs:2516-2539). No row specifies alignment, range, misses or flight time.

rows.acceptance: High-sec and wormhole moons contain only R4/Ubiquitous ores; low-sec and null-sec moons may contain R4-R64. A fractured field mixes the basic and improved (+15%) quality of each ore, unless the fracture is a jackpot.
rows.title: Moon ore class distribution by security and quality mix
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.moon-resources is a query row and feat:mining.moon-jackpot covers only the excellent variant. Neither the security-band class restriction nor the improved-quality mix is in any row.

rows.acceptance: In J-space systems, Local lists a pilot only after they speak. Once listed, they stay until every pilot who saw them has left the system or logged off. Simply entering or leaving does not add or remove members. K-space Local is unchanged.
rows.title: Wormhole space delayed Local
rows.why_missing: feat:social.chat-local (FLAGGED_FAKE) covers k-space Local only. No social, chat or wormhole row specifies J-space delayed Local.

rows.title: Mining module target-type and range validation
rows.why_missing: Only the Mercoxit restriction exists (auditor row feat:mining.mercoxit-deep-core-restriction). The implementation identifies ice harvesters by type ID or by the name containing 'Ice' (crates/eve-server/src/services/inventory_fitting.rs:3180). No row requires target-type validation.

rows.acceptance: W-space ore anomalies (Frontier, Perimeter and Core Deposits, per the class site lists) spawn according to wormhole class, can contain ores from every security band, and are lightly guarded by Sleepers.
rows.title: Wormhole ore anomalies
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.ore-anomalies is generic. This tree's claims state that wormhole space gets no modelled ore site, and no row requires J-space ore sites.

rows.acceptance: Fleet Watchlist window allows adding up to 15 fleet members (governed by Fleet Commander / Wing Commander / Squad Commander skills); client receives real-time updates for shield, armor, and structure percentages of watched pilots; clicking an active target broadcast on a watchlist entry initiates target locking; members leaving fleet or grid are updated or grayed out.
rows.title: Fleet Watchlist member tracking and broadcast targeting
rows.why_missing: Coarse fleet rows (feat:fleet.create-fleet, feat:fleet.invite-accept) do not cover the watchlist sub-system, member limits, health synchronization, or broadcast targeting interactions.

rows.acceptance: Fleet commanders set broadcast permissions and scopes (Entire Fleet, Current Wing, Current Squad); supported broadcast types (Need Shield, Need Armor, Need Capacitor, Target, In Position, Warp To, Align To) are delivered only to eligible hierarchy levels; members lacking broadcast rights receive live UserError CannotBroadcastInFleet when attempting restricted broadcasts; broadcast spam cooldowns (2s) are enforced.
rows.title: Fleet broadcast scope permissions and event filtering
rows.why_missing: No existing ledger row covers broadcast scope delegation, permission restrictions, or cooldown enforcement across fleet hierarchy levels.

rows.acceptance: Fleet commanders select a fleet formation shape (Point, Arrow, Sphere, Wall, Diamond) via fleetObjectHandler.SetFleetFormation; initiating a fleet warp positions landing ships at deterministic grid offsets relative to the fleet commander's landing vector and radius, avoiding ship collision bumps while keeping ships within command burst radius.
rows.title: Fleet warp formation layouts and spatial offsets
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.fleet-warp only checks that members warp; stored formations and spatial landing offset calculations are absent from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Individual fleet members toggle their takesFleetWarp setting via fleetObjectHandler.SetTakesFleetWarp(bool); when disabled, incoming fleet, wing, or squad warp commands leave the member in their current movement mode without initiating warp, and notify the commander that the member ignored fleet warp.
rows.title: Individual member takes-fleet-warp toggle
rows.why_missing: No row models the individual opt-out flag from fleet warp, which is critical for scouts, cyno ships, and logistics anchors.

rows.acceptance: Unprovoked aggression against non-suspect capsuleers in high-sec triggers CONCORD intervention with system security response delays: 0.5 = 19s (±1s), 0.6 = 14s, 0.7 = 11s, 0.8 = 8s, 0.9 = 6s, 1.0 = 6s; CONCORD ships spawn on grid, apply 100% web, warp scramble, capacitor drain, and ECM jam, and destroy the criminal ship; CONCORD hulls are completely invulnerable to damage.
rows.title: CONCORD response delay scaling by system security and combat suite
rows.why_missing: feat:crimewatch.concord-response is a 1-line coarse row that omits exact security-tier delay timings and CONCORD's combat electronic warfare suite.

rows.acceptance: Activating any offensive module (turret, missile launcher, offensive electronic warfare, energy neutralizer, smartbomb, bomb launcher) or issuing offensive drone attack commands initiates a 60-second Weapons Timer; while active, attempting to dock at stations/structures, jump stargates/wormholes, or eject/swap ships is refused with live UserError CannotDockWithWeaponsTimer or CannotJumpWithWeaponsTimer.
rows.title: Weapons timer 60s dock, gate-jump, and ship-eject lockout
rows.why_missing: Only docking mentions weapons timer incidentally; the central 60s timer and its jump/eject/dock lockout gates lack a dedicated testable row in feat:crimewatch.

rows.acceptance: Looting an unowned yellow wreck or cargo container, taking items from another player's unanchored mobile tractor unit, or linking to an Encounter Surveillance System (ESS) Main Bank hack activates a 15-minute Suspect Timer; any other capsuleer in space may freely attack the suspect without CONCORD retaliation or security status penalty.
rows.title: Suspect timer 15-minute flag from unowned loot and ESS theft
rows.why_missing: Existing feat:crimewatch.suspect-flag is coarse and omits ESS main bank interaction, MTU looting, and free engagement rules.

rows.acceptance: Returning fire against a suspect or criminal attacker, or accepting a direct duel challenge via crimewatch.SendDuelChallenge, creates a 5-minute Limited Engagement between the two characters; each subsequent offensive action between the participants resets the timer to 5 minutes; allows combat anywhere in high-sec without sentry gun or CONCORD interference.
rows.title: Limited engagement mutual combat timer and duel lifecycle
rows.why_missing: feat:crimewatch.limited-engagements is a single sentence lacking duel handshake, refresh-on-attack, and sentry gun exclusion semantics.

rows.acceptance: Server strictly enforces character safety setting (Green, Yellow, Red); Green blocks offensive module activation against non-criminals, looting yellow containers, and activating AOE ECM/smartbombs in empire space with UserError CantDoInCurrentSafetyLevel; Yellow permits suspect actions but blocks criminal actions in high-sec; Red permits all actions.
rows.title: Safety switch level server-side validation and action refusal
rows.why_missing: Existing feat:crimewatch.safety-settings only mentions SetSafetyLevel RPC; server-side refusal of illegal module activations and looting under safety rules is not specified.

rows.acceptance: Entering an Abyssal pocket applies the storm weather dogma effects across all player and NPC ships: Electrical (-50% EM shield resist, +50% EM armor resist, +50% cap recharge rate); Dark (+50% ship velocity, -50% turret optimal & falloff); Exotic (-50% Kinetic shield resist, +50% Kinetic armor resist, +50% scan resolution); Firestorm (+50% armor HP, -50% thermal resist); Gamma (+50% shield HP, -50% explosive resist).
rows.title: Abyssal Deadspace weather dogma modifiers
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.abyssal-weather only mentions weather generically; the exact 5 pairs of resistance and performance modifiers applied to all pocket grids are unspecified.

rows.acceptance: Entering the radius of spatial clouds in an Abyssal pocket applies environmental status effects: Tachyon Cloud (+300% max velocity, +300% signature radius bloom); Bioluminescent Cloud (-300% signature radius, -50% velocity); Filament Cloud (-40% shield booster duration and cycle time); effects expire immediately upon leaving the cloud boundary.
rows.title: Abyssal Deadspace environmental cloud hazards
rows.why_missing: No ledger row defines the environmental cloud hazards that dictate piloting trajectories in Abyssal Deadspace.

rows.acceptance: Automata Suppressors and Multibody Tracking Pylons pulse periodic area-of-effect impacts: Suppressors deal explosive damage to all missiles, drones, and small craft within range (Small: 15 km, Medium: 25 km, Large: 40 km); Tracking Pylons grant a tracking speed bonus to all ships and sentries within their radius.
rows.title: Abyssal automated pylons and missile/drone suppression
rows.why_missing: Pylon combat interactions and small-craft suppression are completely omitted from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Every Abyssal Deadspace instance enforces an immutable 20-minute countdown timer starting from initial gate transit; if the character does not exit through the origin gate in the 3rd room before expiration, the pocket collapses, instantly destroying the ship and capsule clone with no insurance payout and logging death to Abyssal Environment.
rows.title: Abyssal 20-minute countdown collapse and destruction
rows.why_missing: Neither abyssal-pocket nor abyssal-tiers tests the fatal expiration consequence of the 20-minute timer.

rows.acceptance: Each Abyssal room contains a Bioadaptive Cache or Triglavian Extraction Sub-node; destroying the cache produces a container with tier-appropriate rewards: mutaplasmids (Decayed/Gravid/Unstable), Triglavian survey databases, filaments, and zero-point condensate; caches in higher tiers (T5/T6) have higher hull HP and require high-DPS application.
rows.title: Abyssal Bioadaptive Cache destruction and loot drop
rows.why_missing: No ledger row defines the cache entity, its destruction gate, or its mutaplasmid loot distribution.

rows.acceptance: The Triglavian Transfer Conduit leading to the next room or origin space spawns in a locked, invulnerable state; defeating every hostile NPC entity on grid triggers a room clear event that unlocks the conduit; activating the unlocked gate transitions the session to the next room pocket.
rows.title: Abyssal Triglavian gate unlocking upon room completion
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.abyssal-gates does not specify the locking mechanic or the requirement that every NPC must be destroyed to unlock transit.

rows.acceptance: FW systems dynamically calculate operational status based on warzone graph adjacency: Frontline (directly borders an enemy-held system, 100% LP/VP payouts, spawns all site tiers); Command Operation (adjacent to a Frontline, 75% LP/VP); Rearguard (borders only friendly/allied systems, 50% LP/VP, site capture counts reduced).
rows.title: Faction Warfare Frontline, Command Operation, and Rearguard system states
rows.why_missing: The V24.01 Frontlines system hierarchy is completely absent from existing feat:fw.* rows.

rows.acceptance: FW complex acceleration gates enforce hull class restrictions: Novice (T1 and Navy Frigates only; Pirate/T2 frigates rejected); Small (Frigates and Destroyers); Medium (Cruisers and below); Large (Battleships and below); Open (all ships); attempting to activate with an ineligible hull returns live UserError ShipTooLargeForGate or ShipTypeNotAllowedInComplex.
rows.title: Faction Warfare complex acceleration gate ship restrictions
rows.why_missing: Existing feat:fw.fw-capture does not model ship restriction tiers across Novice, Small, Medium, Large, and Open complexes.

rows.acceptance: System advantage (0..100%) modifies contested point acquisition for each militia; completing Supply Caches, Listening Posts, and Propaganda Communication sites increases friendly advantage; higher advantage proportionally reduces the number of complex captures required to push a system into vulnerability.
rows.title: Faction Warfare system advantage modifier progression
rows.why_missing: The Advantage system introduced in Uprising/V24 is completely absent from all ledger rows.

rows.acceptance: When a FW system reaches 100% contested, its Infrastructure Hub (I-Hub) becomes vulnerable to direct attack; destroying the I-Hub transfers system sovereignty to the capturing faction; militia pilots donate LP to the I-Hub to upgrade the system Tier (1 to 5), applying proportional market tax reductions and station facility bonuses.
rows.title: Faction Warfare Infrastructure Hub capture and system upgrade tiers
rows.why_missing: No row models the I-Hub vulnerability trigger at 100% contested, sovereignty flipping, or LP tier upgrade progression.

rows.acceptance: Each wormhole jump reduces the wormhole's remaining mass by the exact ship mass (including propulsion module mass additions); wormhole state displays 'This wormhole has not yet had its stability significantly disrupted' (>50% mass remaining); transitions to 'This wormhole has had its stability reduced by ships passing through it' (10-50%); transitions to 'This wormhole has had its stability critically disrupted' (<10%); collapses immediately if a jump exceeds remaining mass.
rows.title: Wormhole mass limit reduction and stability state transitions
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.wormhole-jump (FLAGGED_FAKE) only tests calling JumpWormhole; mass reduction math, stability transitions, and mass collapse lack a dedicated testable row.

rows.acceptance: Wormholes track elapsed time against total lifespan (16h, 24h, 36h, 48h per type); show-info reports: 'This wormhole is beginning to decay, and probably won't last another day' (>24h), 'This wormhole is not yet beginning to decay' (4h-24h), 'This wormhole is reaching the end of its natural lifetime' (<4h); upon timer expiration, both wormhole entrance and exit balls despawn.
rows.title: Wormhole natural lifespan stages and collapse
rows.why_missing: Wormhole temporal lifespan progression and natural collapse are not represented in any ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Wormhole systems with special phenomena apply Dogma modifiers across all ships in the solar system based on system class: Wolf-Rayet (armor HP bonus, small turret damage bonus, signature reduction, shield resist penalty); Pulsar (shield capacity bonus, signature radius penalty, armor resist penalty, capacitor recharge penalty); Magnetar (damage multiplier bonus, missile explosion radius penalty, tracking penalty); Cataclysmic Variable (remote repair bonus, local repair penalty, capacitor recharge penalty).
rows.title: Wormhole system environmental phenomena Dogma modifiers
rows.why_missing: feat:dogma.system-wide-effects is a generic query row; the specific class-scaled environmental effects for Wolf-Rayet, Pulsar, Magnetar, and Cataclysmic Variable are absent.

rows.acceptance: Every wormhole solar system has assigned static connection types defined in SDE; when a static wormhole collapses due to mass or time exhaustion, a new cosmic signature of the identical static wormhole type immediately spawns at a random celestial location in the system, maintaining persistent topological connectivity.
rows.title: Static wormhole connection automatic respawn upon collapse
rows.why_missing: No row models static wormhole replenishment upon collapse.

rows.acceptance: Initiating a hack on a relic or data container generates a hexagonal node grid; exploring adjacent unvisited nodes reveals contents: empty nodes, defensive subroutines (Firewall, Anti-Virus, Core), or utility elements (Self-Repair, Polarity Inversion, Secondary Vector); undiscovered nodes provide distance-indicator clues to the System Core.
rows.title: Relic and Data hacking hexagonal node network generation
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.hacking-minigame is a 1-line row; the node generation, distance clue heuristics, and network traversal lack a testable row.

rows.acceptance: Player virus coherence (health) and virus strength (attack) scale from analyzer module stats (T1: 20 strength / 40-60 coherence; T2: 30 strength / 80-100 coherence) plus Hacking / Archaeology skills (+10 coherence per level); attacking a defensive node subtracts player virus strength from node coherence while node attack subtracts from player coherence; hack fails if player coherence reaches 0.
rows.title: Hacking coherence and virus strength combat calculations
rows.why_missing: The combat math between virus strength/coherence and defensive nodes is completely omitted from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Failing a hack attempt twice on a relic or data site container in null-sec, low-sec, or wormhole space triggers container self-destruction; all contained loot items are destroyed, and an explosive blast inflicts 2,000-5,000 HP area-of-effect damage to any ship within 5,000 meters.
rows.title: Exploration container self-destruction on repeated hack failure
rows.why_missing: No ledger row specifies the 2-failure container detonation and area-of-effect damage mechanics.

rows.acceptance: Installing a Blueprint Copying job on a BPO creates Blueprint Copies (BPCs) with specified runs up to the blueprint's max runs per copy; job duration and cost scale with base copy time, character Science and Industry skills, and facility bonuses; original BPO remains locked until job delivery.
rows.title: Blueprint copying job installation and BPC output
rows.why_missing: Existing industry rows cover manufacturing and facilities, but Blueprint Copying (creating BPCs from BPOs) has no testable row.

rows.acceptance: Installing Material Efficiency (ME) research improves blueprint ME level from 0 up to 10; each ME level reduces required base manufacturing materials by 1% (up to 10% maximum reduction); job installation cost and duration scale with laboratory facility bonuses and system research cost index.
rows.title: Blueprint Material Efficiency research levels 1 to 10
rows.why_missing: feat:industry.install-job does not specify ME research levels, cost index integration, or the 1..10% material reduction curve.

rows.acceptance: Installing Time Efficiency (TE) research improves blueprint TE level from 0 up to 20 (in steps of 2%); each TE level reduces base manufacturing job duration by 2% (up to 20% maximum reduction); job installation cost and duration scale with laboratory facility bonuses and system research cost index.
rows.title: Blueprint Time Efficiency research levels 1 to 20
rows.why_missing: TE research levels and the 2..20% duration reduction curve are absent from all industry rows.

rows.acceptance: Installing an Invention job consumes a Tech I BPC, two Datacore types matching the item's science groups, and an optional Decryptor; success chance is computed from base hull probability (Frigates 40%, Cruisers 34%, Battleships 30%), character science skills, and decryptor modifier; successful invention delivers a Tech II BPC with calculated runs, ME, and TE.
rows.title: Tech II Invention probability, datacores, and decryptor modifiers
rows.why_missing: Tech II Invention (the core mechanism for T2 production in EVE) has no row in feat:industry.*.

rows.acceptance: Applying an Abyssal Mutaplasmid (Decayed, Gravid, Unstable) to an eligible module type consumes the mutaplasmid and rolls each mutable Dogma attribute independently within the mutaplasmid's defined percentile bounds; creates an un-repackageable dynamic singleton item with custom attribute mappings and unique type ID.
rows.title: Abyssal Mutaplasmid dynamic item mutation
rows.why_missing: Mutaplasmid item mutation (Abyssal rolling) is completely missing from all module, industry, and dogma rows.

rows.acceptance: Deploying a Command Center on a planet establishes baseline CPU and Power Grid; training Command Center Upgrades permits upgrading the CC level (1 to 6), expanding available grid/CPU budget; installing pins (extractors, factories, storage, spaceports, links) deducts from this budget and refuses placement if budget is exceeded.
rows.title: Planetary command center level CPU and power grid budget
rows.why_missing: feat:pi.pins only mentions placing pins; the Command Center upgrade progression (levels 1-6) and CPU/Powergrid budget enforcement are not covered.

rows.acceptance: Installing an Extractor Control Unit (ECU) program deploys up to 10 heads across a planet's resource density map; extraction yield per cycle scales with the local resource density under each head and chosen program length (1 hour to 14 days); output displays a characteristic time-decay curve with higher hourly yield on shorter programs.
rows.title: Extractor Control Unit head survey density and output decay
rows.why_missing: feat:pi.extractor-program does not model the 10 extractor heads, spatial hotspot density overlaps, or program-duration decay curves.

rows.acceptance: Basic, Advanced, and High-Tech factories require installing a matching schematic (P0->P1, P1->P2, P2->P3, P3->P4); input commodities must be explicitly routed from storage/extractors to factory inputs, and output commodities routed to storage or launchpads; factories idle with UserError if inputs are depleted or output destination is full.
rows.title: Planetary factory schematic routing and commodities production
rows.why_missing: feat:pi.factory-cycles only checks that cycles run; explicit commodity route configuration, schematic assignment, and buffer blockage rules are not specified.

rows.acceptance: Transferring commodities between a planetary launchpad and a Planetary Customs Office (POCO) assesses export/import taxes: tax = commodity base market value * quantity * tax rate; NPC POCO applies 10% base tax; player-owned POCO applies corporation tax rate with standing discounts; transfers fail if character cannot pay required ISK.
rows.title: Planetary Customs Office import and export taxation
rows.why_missing: feat:pi.customs-office only mentions tax rate lookup; the actual tax formula based on commodity tier base values and transfer execution is absent.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Cynosural Field Generator consumes Liquid Ozone fuel based on ship hull and Cynosural Field Theory skill; creates a celestial cynosural beacon ball visible system-wide on the overview; the activating ship is completely immobilized (speed 0 m/s) and cannot dock, jump, or cloak for the 5-minute cycle duration.
rows.title: Cynosural Field Generator beacon spawning and ship immobilization
rows.why_missing: No row models cynosural beacon ball creation, Liquid Ozone consumption, or the 5-minute immobilization lock.

rows.acceptance: Covert Cynosural Field Generators activate on Stealth Bombers, Force Recons, Blockade Runners, and Black Ops hulls without consuming Liquid Ozone; creates a covert cynosural beacon visible only to fleet members; duration is 1 minute; permits jumping and bridging by Black Ops and Covert Jump Portals.
rows.title: Covert Cynosural Field beacon generation for Black Ops
rows.why_missing: Covert cyno mechanics (zero fuel, fleet-only visibility, 1-minute cycle, covert portal targeting) are completely missing from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Activating jump drive consumes racial isotope fuel per light-year jumped based on ship type and Jump Fuel Conservation skill; jump activation adds a Jump Activation Cooldown timer and scales Jump Fatigue minutes: fatigue = (current fatigue * 0.1 max 10 min + 1) * (1 + distance_ly * ship_fatigue_multiplier); jump is refused if jump range exceeds ship maximum.
rows.title: Capital ship jump drive fuel consumption and fatigue accumulation
